tara-sales: FYI customer wants a short POC: swap their legacy streaming ingest to our SDK-based streaming with function calls + structured JSON output. They want minimal code changes on their side. Any gotchas?
owen-se: Usually two pain points: connection semantics (SSE vs WS) and backpressure. If they use long-lived connections we need client-side buffering + reconnect logic. Which SDK (lang) are they using?
tara-sales: Theyuse Python backend + a Node frontend for admin tools.
lia-ml: For structured outputs + tool calls we recommend using our SDK call patterns rather than raw HTTP so the tool-call hooks are handled. Python SDK has a streaming generator with on_function_call callback. Node SDK supports streaming events too.
ben-devops: From infra side: if we route their traffic through our proxy during cutover we must support idempotent request IDs and dedupe during fan-out. Also watch socket limits if they open 500 concurrent SSEs.
owen-se: Suggestion for minimal change: give them a shim library (1-file) that implements the same function signatures they already have but internally switches to our streaming client. Example shim snippet for Python:```python
# shim.py
from redwood_sdk import Client
c = Client(api_key=ENV["POC_KEY"]) 
def stream_generate(req_iter):
    for chunk in c.stream(req_iter, model="x" ):
        if chunk.get("function_call"):
            handle_function(chunk)
        yield chunk
```
Use that to avoid touching business logic.
tara-sales: Nice. Buyer asked about reliability: what if our hosted spikes and they need to fallback to local lightweight model?
lia-ml: We can run a local quantized fallback (LLM-lite) in their infra or use a cached-response fallback. For session continuity across fallback we need to forward the same conversation history and maintain token window management. We'll document a hybrid fallback flow.
ben-devops: Security: they require audit logs + ability to revoke keys. For demo we can supply scoped ephemeral keys and a webhook to push logs to their SIEM. Also they asked about ingress IP allowlist; we can provide our egress IP ranges for their firewall.
owen-se: For tool calls (their fraud API), prefer a reverse-auth proxy pattern: we call their stub endpoint which validates an HMAC and returns a token for backend use. That way we never store prod creds. Demo can run stub in our env.
tara-sales: Pricing concern: they asked if demo will incur Dedicated costs if we pre-warm nodes.
ben-devops: We can pre-warm using small burst-only reserved capacity (no long commit), or run hosted with aggressive caching. Estimate needed: what's peak tokens/min?
owen-se: Ask them for 24 sample requests. I'll run quick token sims. As a rough rule: average request 80 tokens -> 50 rps = 240k tokens/min -> 14.4M tokens/hr. That affects cost a lot. For streaming structured responses add ~15% overhead.
tara-sales: Action items: Owen to produce token sim + shim example, Lia to prepare SDK quickstart (Python + Node) and sample function-call stub, Ben to collect IP ranges + logging options, I'll confirm schedule with customer for a mid-May demo.
infra-bot: NOTE: Demo infra ticket created -> POC-7821. Cluster spin target: 2025-05-14T09:00:00Z.
lia-ml: I'll also include acceptance tests: 1) structured JSON conforms to their schema for 30 cases, 2) tool-call handshake succeeds in sandbox 95% of runs, 3) median end-to-end latency under 300ms for 95% of sample requests.
owen-se: Quick cURL example for their engineers to try (non-sdk):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $POC_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"stream":true, "model":"redwood-mini","functions":[{"name":"fraud_check","schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"score":{"type":"number"}}}}]}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Explain that raw HTTP works but SDKs handle reconnects + function callbacks more gracefully.
tara-sales: Good. Please keep messages short in the runbook. I'll send a 20-min sync invite for Friday to run through runbook and decide stub vs real proxy.
ben-devops: I'll add revocation steps and cron for key rotation in the runbook.
lia-ml: Also adding a small test harness (pytest) that asserts schema match for each gold sample.
owen-se: I'll drop the shim + token sim into the shared drive by EOD.
tara-sales: Thanks everyone. :rocket:
